questions.question: Did I wake up today feeling tired, honestly?

note.title: When checking in with yourself, consider:
points: How alert and ready do I feel mentally?
How good was my sleep last night?
Did I feel the need to hit the snooze button today on the alarm?
Did I need a cup of coffee to get myself going?

questions.question: How recovered does my body feel following the prior workout?

note.body: Perform a quick body scan, examining both muscle and joint soreness/achiness. Are your muscles so sore that to the touch you could scream “ouch!”, or does it feel more mild and tolerable? If you are so sore and achy that you feel it will hamper today's training session, select “Not at all”.

questions.question: Did I wake up with water retention, bloating, diarrhea, or constipation?

note.title: Water retention occurs when excess fluids build up inside the body. A few of the ways this may show up:
points: Unexplained weight fluctuations in a short period of time
Your ring doesn’t fit anymore, or your stomach feels swollen
When pressed, your skin may hold an indent for a few seconds
Swollen or stiff joints
Constipation: do I feel complete after my bowel movement? Are my stools infrequent, hard, dry, or difficult to pass?

questions.question: My overall stress level today is?

options.label: Moderate — I’m experiencing some stress, but managing well

note.body: Stress isn’t always a bad thing, however, when it occurs at a level that we cannot manage effectively, over time it can become a problem. Ask yourself honestly: “what areas of my life (both personally and professionally) are feeling most stressed right now, and to what degree are they affecting me?”

questions.question: My willingness and motivation level for training today is?

note.body: Do you feel excited to get after it today? Are you itching to move your body and get under those bells? If not, that’s ok, we all have those days — however, consider exploring why. Explore the question: “what things are draining my zest for life and motivation to train today?”

rules.name: Recovery Day
rules.message: It is suggested that today be a day for Stretching and/or Working In. You can find these corresponding videos in your Program Library, or on any prior recovery day in the Program. Allow gentle movement, breath, and restorative activities guide your personal practice today.

rules.name: Off Day
rules.message: It is suggested today be a day for total and complete rest from training. This would be a great time for a brief nap (~20 minutes), easy walk, massage, and/or anything you can do to relax and restore your body.

Ask yourself honestly: “what areas of my life (both personally and professionally) are feeling most stressed right now, and to what degree are they affecting me?”

questions.question: My willingness and motivation level for training today is?

note.body: Do you feel excited to get after it today? Are you itching to move your body and get under those bells? If not, that’s ok, we all have those days — however, consider exploring why. Explore the question: “what things are draining my zest for life and motivation to train today?”

questions.question: Did I wake up today feeling tired, honestly?

note.title: When checking in with yourself, consider:
points: How alert and ready do I feel mentally?

questions.question: How recovered does my body feel following the prior workout?

note.body: Perform a quick body scan, examining both muscle and joint soreness/achiness. Are your muscles so sore that to the touch you could scream “ouch!”, or does it feel more mild and tolerable? If you are so sore and achy that you feel it will hamper today's training session, select “Not at all”.

questions.question: Did I wake up with water retention, bloating, diarrhea, or constipation?

note.title: Water retention occurs when excess fluids build up inside the body. A few of the ways this may show up:
points: Unexplained weight fluctuations in a short period of time
Your ring doesn’t fit anymore, or your stomach feels swollen
When pressed, your skin may hold an indent for a few seconds
Swollen or stiff joints
Constipation: do I feel complete after my bowel movement? Are my stools infrequent, hard, dry, or difficult to pass?

scenarios.summary: Begin on the lightest bell and earn the next one. Technique first, load second.

stretchTest.title: Stretch Test
stretchTest.tagline: Check the positions the program demands
stretchTest.description: Five self-assessments covering hips, ankles, shoulders and t-spine. You get a mobility profile and the exact drills to prioritise.

questions.question: Standing with straight legs, how far do your hands reach?

options.label: Fingertips or palms to the floor

questions.question: Can you sit into a deep squat with heels down?

options.label: No — heels lift or I fall back

questions.question: Lying on your back, can you press your arms overhead to the floor with ribs down?

options.label: No — my ribs flare or arms stop short

questions.question: Knee-to-wall ankle test: how far from the wall is your toe?
Seated, how freely can you rotate your upper back each way?

options.label: Stiff and uneven side to side

bands.title: Restricted — mobility first
bands.summary: Several positions the program relies on are not available yet. That is fixable, and quickly.
points: Run the daily mobility minimums before every session.
Stay in Phase 1 until the toe touch and ankle test improve.
Retake this test in two weeks.

bands.title: Workable — train and maintain
bands.summary: You can train the full program safely with targeted maintenance work.
points: Ten minutes of mobility before each session.
Prioritise whichever test scored lowest for you.
Retake this test monthly.

bands.title: Open — keep it
bands.summary: You have the range the program asks for. The job now is keeping it.
points: Short mobility flow on rest days is enough.
Move straight into Phase 2 when your strength base allows.
Retake this test each quarter.

courseMeta.title: Kettlebell Lifestyle Beginner
courseMeta.tagline: Nine weeks to a kettlebell you can trust
courseMeta.description: Kettlebell Lifestyle is a 9-week personalised, multi-level kettlebell and wellness program. Level I teaches the swing variations, squats, presses, cleans and combination movements from the ground up — alongside morning routines, personalised stretching, bodyweight warm-ups and follow-along workouts.
outcomes: Execute beginner-level kettlebell movements safely and efficiently
Spot the common lifting mistakes and fix them on the spot
Follow a balanced, structured program from warm-up to cooldown
Build a morning and mobility habit that survives a busy week
format: 9 weeks across four phases — On Ramp, Phase 1, Phase 2 and Phase 3
61 numbered days: workout, recovery, skill development and a final Challenge Day
Follow-along workouts with on-screen timers and scaling options
Downloadable phase plans so you can train away from the screen
whatsNeeded: One kettlebell — use the Kettlebell Selector if you're unsure
A mat and roughly 2m x 2m of floor space
A wall or doorway for mobility drills

courseMeta.title: Kettlebell Lifestyle Intermediate
courseMeta.tagline: Heavier bells, longer chains, real capacity
courseMeta.description: Level II picks up where the Beginner program ends. Denser conditioning, double-bell work, snatch progressions and complexes — with the same morning routine, warm-up and stretching structure holding it all together.
outcomes: Chain movements into complexes without losing position
Progress load and density on purpose instead of by feel
Own the get-up, snatch and double-bell work
Manage fatigue with deliberate deload and restore days
format: 9 weeks across four phases — On Ramp, Phase 1 (plus a Preparation Day), Phase 2 and Phase 3
Heavier strength blocks paired with pacing-based conditioning
Skill sessions dedicated to snatch and complex technique
Deload and restore days built into every phase
whatsNeeded: Two kettlebells of the same weight where possible
A mat and clear overhead space
Completed Level I or equivalent kettlebell experience
